g_verbIrr: Irregular ({u}): learn the past forms by heart: {a} · {b}
g_verbReg: Regular: the simple past takes {te} and the participle {ge}: {a} · {b}
g_sep: Separable: in the present the prefix {p} goes to the end of the sentence: {ex} — in the participle {ge} goes in the middle: {pp}
g_modal: Modal verb: the main verb goes to the end as an infinitive: {ex}
g_perfSein: Perfekt with {aux}, because it shows movement or a change of state: {ex}
g_akk: In the accusative ({akk}) only the masculine article changes: {a} · {b}
g_weak: A "weak" noun ({nd}): it takes {en} in every case except the nominative: {a}
g_plural: Plural: {pl} — in the {dat} plural it adds {n}: {ex}
g_sub: Subordinating conjunction: the conjugated verb goes to the end.
g_subEx: Subordinating conjunction: the conjugated verb goes to the end: {ex}
g_coord: Joins two sentences without changing word order (position zero): {ex}
g_personal: Personal pronoun, it changes with its role in the sentence: {ex}
g_wq: In a {wf} the question word comes first and the verb second.
g_wqEx: In a {wf} the question word comes first and the verb second: {ex}
g_adv: An adverb doesn't change. If it starts the sentence, the verb follows straight after it (position two) and the subject comes after the verb.
g_nicht: {n} negates verbs, adjectives and adverbs; nouns are negated with {k}: {ex}
